messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on continuous-batch path in eu-west-1. SLO p99 breached for streaming API for the last 6m. Affected services: streaming.generate, stream-completions. Paging oncall.
Aisha (oncall): on it. seeing the PD page. quick context pls — is this mixed-seqlen or KV churn?
Ben (eng): preliminary traces show a lot of large batches waiting ~120ms for packing, then single huge execs. mixed sequence lengths + a few very long seqs. tail amplification.
Carmen (sre): I can confirm KV cache evictions around the same time. nodes in pool 3 had elevated mem pressure -> more GC + slower response. likely combined effect.
Aisha (oncall): ok. customer impact? any errors or just latency?
Marta (prod): streaming customers are seeing stalls (client timeouts) and partial frames delivered. error rate up ~0.3% for streaming endpoints in eu-west-1. Mobile partner "BlueApps" reported degraded UX.
Aisha (oncall): good. urgency: paging remains. Ben, can we do a live mitigation that doesn't require model restarts?
Ben (eng): yes. short list: 1) reduce continuous_batch.pack_size_target from 64 -> 32 for streaming route to avoid waiting; 2) lower continuous_batch.max_wait_ms  from 100 -> 30; 3) enable strict preemptive scheduling for streaming (favor streaming over background batch jobs); 4) pin long-seqlen customers to a separate pool if possible.
Carmen (sre): also suggest a temporary KV cache warm-up disable policy for index eviction to avoid churn. I can patch cache eviction threshold on the fly.
Aisha (oncall): do those sound safe to apply regionally? we want minimal blast radius.
Ben (eng): yes apply to eu-west-1 streaming nodepool only. canary on 1 node first, then 25%, 100%. I have the rollout script.
Ben (eng): quick command to change live config (canary):
```
curl -X POST https://console.internal.redwood/api/v1/runtime/configs/patch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"selector":"nodepool:eu-west-1-streaming","patch":{"continuous_batch.pack_size_target":32,"continuous_batch.max_wait_ms":30,"scheduling.mode":"stream-first"}}'
```
Aisha (oncall): Carmen can you run the canary and watch metrics? I'll notify on-call list and PD.
Carmen (sre): starting canary on node euw-s-03 now. tail latency dash streaming.p99 for that node.
Carmen (sre): canary metrics: p99 dropped from 910ms -> 420ms on euw-s-03 within 30s. no increase in error rate.
Marta (prod): BlueApps confirmed slight improvement on the canary traffic they were routed to. Good sign.
Aisha (oncall): roll to 25% next. Ben, make sure pack_size_backpressure is disabled for the first minute to avoid oscillation.
Ben (eng): acknowledged. patching backpressure config to 0 for canary window. rolling to 25% (euw-s-0[4-06]).
incident-bot: DEPLOY: config-patch-1748123456 rolled to 25% (3 nodes).
Carmen (sre): 25% results: region p99 dropped ~48% overall, no significant KV churn observed so far. tail executions count decreased.
Aisha (oncall): continue to 100% with 2m observation. also open a mitigation task: isolate very long-seq requests to a separate tenant pool to avoid future amplification.
Ben (eng): creating task: TASK-16842 "tenant-isolation-longseq" and a short-term scheduler change. I'll also add metrics alert watch for pack wait > 50ms per node.
Marta (prod): we should message impacted customers now (BlueApps + two internal partners). draft msg: "We're investigating elevated streaming latency in eu-west-1; we've deployed mitigations that have reduced p99 by ~50% and will monitor closely. Ops contact: oncall@redwood." Approve?
Aisha (oncall): send. add note that root cause suspected mixed sequence lengths + cache thrash.
Ben (eng): follow-up actions: 1) full root-cause trace across batcher for the window 14:10-14:30 UTC; 2) KV cache tuning rollback plan; 3) implement strict-seq-length-routing in 2 weeks and add canary config to rollout tool.
Carmen (sre): I'll attach continuity logs and GC traces to TASK-16842 and set retention for 14 days.
Aisha (oncall): PagerDuty: please escalate to severity 2 until we confirm stable. @PagerDuty
PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged. Severity set to 2. Notifications escalated to SRE leads.
Marta (prod): customer communication sent. BlueApps replied: "thanks — performance back to usable for now, please advise when full fix ready."
Aisha (oncall): good. unassigning oncall in 1h if metrics stable. final notes: we should consider adding automatic batch-flushing for streaming requests when a very long sequence is detected to avoid starve-wait amplification.
Ben (eng): agree. will prototype auto-flush + length-based routing. timeline: prototype by EOW.
Carmen (sre): leaving monitoring on. will update in TASK-16842.
Aisha (oncall): thanks team. closing live page when region p99 <= 300ms for 15m.
incident-bot: RESOLVED: SLO breach mitigated by config rollouts; monitoring ongoing.
Aisha (oncall): closing thread after postmortem. adding postmortem owner Ben.
Ben (eng): assigned. will start root-cause doc and schedule a 30m follow-up with SRE + Prod tomorrow.
